Chemical Energetics — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.

mcqs.q: When a stress shifts an equilibrium, does the system fully undo the change?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
The system shifts to completely cancel the change and return concentrations to their original values.
No — Le Chatelier's principle says the system PARTIALLY opposes the change; equilibrium shifts to a new position that minimises but doesn't eliminate the disturbance.
